views.name: movie_basic

params.description: One-row-per-movie basic attributes: returns movie id, title, year, rating, and vote count for each movie.
params.when_to_use: Fetch basic movie metadata (title, year) along with numeric rating and vote count for display or filtering. | Compose into downstream analyses that need one aggregated row per movie (e.g., joining to genre counts, cast aggregates, or computing additional per-movie metrics). | Serve as the grain table when building higher-level aggregations by movie (e.g., average rating by year after grouping by the view's MID).
params.output_schema: MID: unique movie identifier — directly from Movie.MID | title: movie title string — directly from Movie.title | year: release year (likely integer) — directly from Movie.year | rating: movie rating (numeric, e.g., average user rating) — directly from Movie.rating | num_votes: number of votes supporting rating (integer) — directly from Movie.num_votes
params.metric: rating = Movie.rating  -- base numeric attribute (no aggregation in this view) | num_votes = Movie.num_votes  -- base numeric attribute (no aggregation in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_with_genres on MID — safe because movie_basic is one-row-per-MID and movie_with_genres is a JOIN view that must be treated as potentially one-to-many (genres). If movie_with_genres is already one-row-per-MID (e.g., aggregated), it is safe; otherwise, joining the raw movie_with_genres (one-to-many) will duplicate rating and num_votes and requires aggregation after the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_with_languages on MID — safe only if movie_with_languages has been pre-aggregated to one-row-per-MID; otherwise it is a one-to-many join and will multiply movie_basic rows and its measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_with_countries on MID — safe only if that view is one-row-per-MID; treat as one-to-many otherwise and re-aggregate to avoid duplicating ratings/votes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_cast_members on MID — do NOT join directly if movie_cast_members is a one-to-many join (casts per movie). Direct join will duplicate rating and num_votes; instead aggregate cast members (for example count distinct cast members per MID) in movie_cast_members or join to an aggregated sibling (people_film_counts) before combining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to people_film_counts on person identifier aggregated by person — safe to join when the key is a person and you intend to attach per-person aggregates (this view remains one-row-per-MID only if joined via a single person key that is one-to-one per movie, otherwise it will expand rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to genre_movie_counts on MID only if genre_movie_counts is aggregated to one-row-per-MID (e.g., a genre summary column); otherwise joining raw genre lists will multiply rows and require re-aggregation. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_rating_rank on MID — safe if movie_rating_rank is one-row-per-MID (a rank per movie). If it is a ranking window that produces one row per movie, joining will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_running_votes on MID — safe if that view produces one-row-per-MID (e.g., running cumulative votes per movie); if it contains multiple rows per MID (different windows), joining will duplicate base measures unless you restrict/aggregate. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_locations on MID — do NOT join directly if movie_locations is many locations per movie; re-aggregate locations to one-row-per-MID before joining to preserve movie_basic's one-row grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_people_roles on MID — do NOT join directly if it lists multiple people/roles per movie; aggregate roles per MID (e.g., role counts or pivot) before joining to avoid multiplying rating/num_votes. | general rule: movie_basic is strictly one-row-per-MID. Any join to a one-to-many sibling view/table that is not pre-aggregated will multiply rows and therefore duplicate the 'rating' and 'num_votes' measures. To compose safely, either (a) join only to views guaranteed to be one-row-per-MID (e.g., ranking or aggregated per-movie views), or (b) perform aggregation (GROUP BY MID) on the one-to-many side before joining, or (c) join and then re-aggregate the result back to MID with appropriate aggregations (e.g., AVG(rating) will be incorrect unless you deduplicate rows).

views.description: Normalized projection of the Movie table that preserves canonical identifiers and key measures. Use this as the clean movie base for joins, aggregations, or ranking. It ensures types are preserved and exposes year, rating, num_votes for downstream calculations. | Use for: List movies with ratings or votes; join movies to genres/people/countries; filter movies by year/rating/votes; compute aggregates per movie.

views.name: movie_with_genres
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  m."year",
  mg."GID",
  g."Name" AS "Name",
  mg."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Genre" mg ON m."MID" = mg."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Genre" g ON mg."GID" = g."GID"

params.description: Provides one row per movie-genre assignment: movie identifiers and basic movie attributes plus the genre id/name for that assignment.
params.when_to_use: List all genres assigned to each movie (movie → genre membership). | Filter or search movies by genre and return movie metadata (title, year). | Compose into aggregations by movie or by genre (e.g., count movies per genre, list movies for a genre). | Use as a building block when joining movie-level data with genre-level data without losing the per-assignment grain.
params.output_schema: MID: movie identifier — derived from Movie.MID (base table Movie."MID"). | title: movie title — derived from Movie.title (base table Movie."title"). | year: movie year (release or recorded year) — derived from Movie.year (base table Movie."year"). | GID: genre identifier for this movie-genre assignment — derived from M_Genre.GID (base table M_Genre."GID"). | Name: genre name (human label) — derived from Genre.Name (base table Genre."Name"). May be NULL when Genre has no matching row because the view LEFT JOINs Genre. | ID: internal id of the movie-genre assignment row — derived from M_Genre.ID (base table M_Genre."ID").
params.grounded_columns: Movie."MID" | Movie."title" | Movie."year" | M_Genre."GID" | M_Genre."ID" | Genre."Name"
params.metric: No derived numeric aggregates are defined in this view. All output columns are direct projections from base columns: MID = Movie."MID", title = Movie."title", year = Movie."year", GID = M_Genre."GID", Name = Genre."Name", ID = M_Genre."ID".
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_basic on MID — safe because movie_basic is one-row-per-MID (normalized movie row), so joining movie_with_genres (grain = [MID,GID]) to movie_basic on MID will not duplicate rows beyond the intended one-row-per-assignment. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to genre_movie_counts on GID — safe if genre_movie_counts is one-row-per-GID (an aggregation keyed by GID). Joining on GID will attach genre-level aggregated metrics without duplicating movie-genre assignment rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to Genre (base table) on GID — redundant for Name but safe; Genre is one-row-per-GID so it will not duplicate rows. Note this view already LEFT JOINs Genre and exposes Genre.Name. | do NOT join without aggregation to movie_cast_members (JOIN) or movie_locations (JOIN) or movie_people_roles (JOIN) directly on MID while expecting measures from this view to remain unduplicated — those sibling views are likely one-to-many from MID (multiple cast members, locations, roles) and will multiply the [MID,GID] rows. Instead, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many side first (e.g., derive per-MID aggregates from movie_cast_members) and then join on MID, or | - join and then re-aggregate grouping back to the desired grain ([MID,GID] or MID) to avoid inflated counts/metrics. | do NOT join directly to people_film_counts or genre_movie_counts if those are multi-row per key (verify they are aggregated to a single row per key). Joining to aggregated single-row-per-key views is safe; joining to raw multi-row tables is not safe. | When composing higher-level aggregates (for example, counting distinct people per movie-genre), treat this view as having grain [MID,GID]: group by MID or GID as needed and apply proper DISTINCT or COUNT aggregation to avoid double-counting if other dimensions are added. | If you need a single-row-per-MID result, aggregate this view by MID (e.g., array_agg(GID) or count(GID)) rather than joining to it and expecting uniqueness.

views.description: Denormalized movie-to-genre relation: one row per movie-genre assignment including human-readable genre Name. Useful for questions about counts or lists of genres per movie, top genres, or filtering movies by genre. | Use for: Which genres a movie belongs to; count movies per genre; filter movies by genre name; list movies for a genre.

views.name: movie_with_languages
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  m."year",
  ml."LAID",
  l."Name" AS "Name",
  ml."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Language" ml ON m."MID" = ml."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Language" l ON ml."LAID" = l."LAID"

params.description: A row-per-movie-per-language view listing each Movie (MID, title, year) together with the language association (LAID, Name, ID) from M_Language and Language.
params.when_to_use: List all languages associated with a given movie (by MID or title). | Filter movies by language (LAID or language Name) while retaining movie attributes. | Compose further aggregations that count languages per movie (must re-aggregate). | Join movie metadata to language-level details when building movie-language level outputs (one row per movie-language pair).
params.output_schema: MID: Movie identifier — derives from Movie.MID (m."MID"). | title: Movie title — derives from Movie.title (m."title"). | year: Movie year — derives from Movie.year (m."year"). | LAID: Language identifier for the movie-language association — derives from M_Language.LAID (ml."LAID"). | Name: Language name — derives from Language.Name (l."Name"). | ID: Identifier of the M_Language row (association ID) — derives from M_Language.ID (ml."ID").
params.grounded_columns: Movie.MID | Movie.title | Movie.year | M_Language.MID | M_Language.LAID | M_Language.ID | Language.LAID | Language.Name
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated metrics. Columns are direct projections: MID = Movie.MID, title = Movie.title, year = Movie.year, LAID = M_Language.LAID, Name = Language.Name, ID = M_Language.ID.
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_basic on MID (movie_with_languages.MID = movie_basic.MID) — safe because movie_basic is one-row-per-MID and will not duplicate the movie_language rows; this view is one-row-per (MID, LAID). | Join to movie_with_genres on MID is NOT safe without care: movie_with_genres is one-row-per (MID, Genre) (a one-to-many relative). Joining movie_with_genres directly to this view will multiply rows for movies that have multiple genres and multiple languages (resulting in cross-product duplication). To combine genre counts with language rows, either (a) aggregate movie_with_genres to one row per MID before joining, or (b) aggregate this view (e.g., count languages per MID) before joining. | Do NOT join directly to movie_cast_members (one-to-many per MID) without re-aggregation first — it will multiply rows when a movie has multiple cast members. If you need movie-level measures (e.g., number of languages) together with cast rows, compute the measure (COUNT DISTINCT LAID) as an aggregation per MID from this view and then join that aggregated result to movie_cast_members. | Joining to Language on LAID is redundant if using the view (Language.Name already included). If you need additional Language attributes not present here, join Language on LAID — safe as Language is one-row-per-LAID (a dimension), so it will not duplicate measures. | Joins to aggregate/snapshot views (people_film_counts, genre_movie_counts, movie_rating_rank, movie_running_votes) are safe only when those views are one-row-per-MID (or per matching key). Verify the sibling view grain before joining. If the sibling view is per-MID, join on MID (safe). If it is aggregated at a different grain (e.g., per-person), aggregate appropriately before joining. | To produce movie-level metrics from this view (e.g., language_count per MID), re-aggregate: language_count = COUNT(DISTINCT LAID) GROUP BY MID. Do not assume one language row equals one movie row — this view intentionally has multiple rows per movie when multiple languages exist. | When composing with dimensions keyed by LAID (Language) you may join on LAID safely because Language is one-row-per-LAID; when composing with dimensions keyed by M_Language.ID, treat M_Language as the association (one row per association) — joining to other M_Language-level data is safe on ID.

views.description: Denormalized movie-to-language relation: one row per movie-language assignment with language Name. Useful for filtering or aggregating movies by language. | Use for: Count movies by language; list movies in a specific language; join languages with ratings/votes.

views.name: movie_with_countries
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  m."year",
  mc."CID",
  c."Name" AS "Name",
  mc."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Country" mc ON m."MID" = mc."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Country" c ON mc."CID" = c."CID"

params.description: Provides movies at the movie × country grain: one row per movie (MID) and associated country (CID), returning movie identifiers and basic movie attributes with the country name and the join-row ID from the M_Country bridge.
params.when_to_use: List all countries associated with each movie (e.g., which countries produced or are associated with a movie). | Filter or group movies by country (e.g., count movies per country, or list movies for a given CID). | Compose further SQL that needs movie-level attributes together with country membership as a dimension (for example, joining to ratings/metrics that are at movie grain). | Use as the starting point for aggregations by movie×country (for example: number of votes or average rating per movie per country) provided downstream aggregation accounts for this grain.
params.output_schema: MID: movie identifier (derived from Movie.MID). The primary movie key included in the view; base column: Movie."MID". | title: movie title (derived from Movie.title). Base column: Movie."title". | year: movie year (derived from Movie.year). Base column: Movie."year". | CID: country identifier associated to the movie (derived from M_Country.CID). Base column: M_Country."CID". | Name: country name for the CID (derived from Country.Name). Base column: Country."Name". | ID: identifier of the M_Country joining row (derived from M_Country.ID). Base column: M_Country."ID".
params.grounded_columns: Movie."MID" | Movie."title" | Movie."year" | M_Country."CID" | M_Country."ID" | Country."CID" | Country."Name"
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated metrics. All columns are direct projections from base tables (no derived aggregates). | If you need metrics per movie×country, define them downstream as aggregates over this view, e.g.: movie_country_vote_count = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE <vote-join-conditions>) when joining to a votes table aggregated appropriately.
params.composition: Safe joins (won't duplicate measures from this view): |  - Join to movie_basic on MID (JOIN movie_basic mb ON movie_with_countries.MID = mb.MID) — safe because movie_basic is normalized to one row per MID, so joining movie_basic to this view preserves the movie×country grain (no duplication of movie-level measures). |  - Join to movie_rating_rank or people_film_counts aggregated at MID (JOIN movie_rating_rank r ON movie_with_countries.MID = r.MID) — safe only if the sibling view/derivation is one-row-per-MID. Verify sibling view grain before joining. |  | Unsafe joins (would duplicate rows/measures unless you re-aggregate): |  - Do NOT directly join to one-to-many movie-level children such as movie_with_genres, movie_with_languages, movie_cast_members, movie_locations, movie_people_roles without re-aggregation, because those sibling views are joins that can have multiple rows per MID and will multiply the movie×country rows (e.g., a movie with 3 countries and 4 genres would produce 12 rows). |  - Do NOT join to people_film_counts, genre_movie_counts, movie_running_votes, or other aggregate/rank/win views that are not guaranteed to be at the same movie×country grain unless they are pre-aggregated to the movie×country grain or you aggregate after joining. |  | Guidance for safe composition when combining with one-to-many data: |  - If you need to combine movie_with_countries with a one-to-many sibling (e.g., genres), either: |    a) aggregate the one-to-many sibling to the movie (or movie×country) grain before joining (e.g., genres_agg = SELECT MID, array_agg(genre) AS genres FROM movie_with_genres GROUP BY MID), then join on MID (or MID+CID if aggregated to movie×country), or |    b) join and then re-aggregate the result to the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY MID, CID to compute counts or other measures) to avoid accidental multiplication. |  | Keys to use: |  - Join on MID to connect movie attributes and movie-level metrics. |  - Join on CID to connect country-level dimensions (e.g., country metadata) — note this view already includes Country.Name via a left join. |  | Cardinality notes: |  - This view's grain is (MID, CID): there may be multiple rows for the same MID if a movie is associated with multiple CID values. Any join that is many-to-one into this view on MID (from a movie-level table) is safe. Any join that is many-to-many or many-from-this-view should be handled by pre-aggregation or post-aggregation to prevent measure duplication.

views.description: Denormalized movie-to-country relation: one row per movie-country assignment with country Name. Use to analyze production countries or filter movies by country. | Use for: Which countries produced a movie; count movies by country; filter movies by country name.

views.name: movie_cast_members
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  mc."PID",
  p."Name" AS "Name",
  p."Gender" AS "Gender",
  mc."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Cast" mc ON m."MID" = mc."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Person" p ON mc."PID" = p."PID"

params.description: Lists every cast member (person) assigned to each movie, returning one row per movie-person casting assignment.
params.when_to_use: Get all cast members for a given movie (by MID or title). | List all movies a given person has been cast in (by PID or Name). | Compose with other movie-level views to add genres, languages, countries, or ratings while preserving one row per movie-person assignment. | Filter or aggregate cast-level counts (e.g., count cast members per movie) by grouping on MID. | Join to person-level details (people_film_counts, movie_people_roles) to enrich cast rows with career aggregates.
params.output_schema: MID: the movie identifier from Movie.MID (m."MID") — grain: part of the view's row identity | title: the movie title from Movie.title (m."title") — informational string for the MID | PID: the person identifier from M_Cast.PID (mc."PID") — grain: part of the view's row identity | Name: person name from Person.Name (p."Name") — nullable (LEFT JOIN), person display label | Gender: person gender from Person.Gender (p."Gender") — nullable (LEFT JOIN), person attribute | ID: the cast-assignment id from M_Cast.ID (mc."ID") — identifier for the specific casting record
params.grounded_columns: Movie.MID | Movie.title | M_Cast.MID | M_Cast.PID | M_Cast.ID | Person.PID | Person.Name | Person.Gender
params.metric: This view is a pure JOIN with no derived numeric aggregations. Derived/expressed columns are identity copies from base tables. | No aggregate metrics are defined in this view. If you need counts, define them by aggregating this view (e.g., cast_count_per_movie = COUNT(*) GROUP BY MID).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_basic on MID — safe because movie_basic is one-row-per-MID (NORM) so it will not duplicate this view's rows/measures; join condition: movie_cast_members.MID = movie_basic.MID | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_with_genres on MID only if movie_with_genres is known to be one-row-per-MID (it is a JOIN view — verify it materializes genres as an array or otherwise one-row-per-MID). If movie_with_genres is one-row-per-MID, join condition: movie_cast_members.MID = movie_with_genres.MID — safe because it won't multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_with_languages or movie_with_countries on MID only if those sibling views are one-row-per-MID (e.g., languages/countries represented as aggregated arrays). If one-row-per-MID, join condition: movie_cast_members.MID = movie_with_languages.MID (or movie_with_countries.MID) — safe. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to people_film_counts on PID — safe because people_film_counts is an AGG (one-row-per-PID), so joining on PID will not duplicate rows; join condition: movie_cast_members.PID = people_film_counts.PID | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_people_roles on (MID, PID) if movie_people_roles is one-row-per-(MID,PID) role summary — safe because it aligns to this view's grain; join condition: movie_cast_members.MID = movie_people_roles.MID AND movie_cast_members.PID = movie_people_roles.PID | do NOT join to a table/view that is one-to-many relative to this view's grain without re-aggregation: for example, do NOT join to a raw MovieGenres or raw MovieLanguages table that contains multiple rows per MID (genres/languages as separate rows) unless you first aggregate those rows to one-row-per-MID (e.g., array_agg) or you plan to re-aggregate the composed result. Otherwise the join will multiply the number of rows for the same (MID,PID) and thus duplicate any measures derived from this view. | do NOT join to sibling aggregate views that are many-per-MID or many-per-PID (e.g., a ranking window that returns multiple rows per MID) unless you restrict/aggregate them to one row per key. If you need to attach a many-side attribute, either (a) aggregate that attribute to one row per MID or PID, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate at the intended output grain (e.g., GROUP BY MID to compute movie-level measures). | If composing higher-level metrics: treat this view's natural measures as row-level facts (one row = one cast assignment). To produce movie-level metrics (cast_count_per_movie), aggregate this view with GROUP BY MID (and include title via MIN(title) or join to movie_basic for stable title). To produce person-level metrics (movies_per_person), aggregate GROUP BY PID.

views.description: Denormalized movie-to-cast relation: one row per movie-cast assignment with person Name and Gender. Useful for actor-centric queries, actor counts per movie, or filtering movies by cast member. | Use for: List actors in a movie; count movies per actor; filter movies by actor gender; join actor info with movie ratings.

views.name: people_film_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p."PID",
  p."Name" AS "Name",
  p."Gender" AS "Gender",
  COALESCE(cast_counts.cast_movie_count, 0) AS "cast_movie_count",
  COALESCE(dir_counts.director_movie_count, 0) AS "director_movie_count",
  COALESCE(prod_counts.producer_movie_count, 0) AS "producer_movie_count"
FROM "Person" p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT "PID", COUNT(DISTINCT "MID") AS cast_movie_count
  FROM "M_Cast"
  GROUP BY "PID"
) cast_counts ON p."PID" = cast_counts."PID"
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT "PID", COUNT(DISTINCT "MID") AS director_movie_count
  FROM "M_Director"
  GROUP BY "PID"
) dir_counts ON p."PID" = dir_counts."PID"
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT "PID", COUNT(DISTINCT "MID") AS producer_movie_count
  FROM "M_Producer"
  GROUP BY "PID"
) prod_counts ON p."PID" = prod_counts."PID"

params.description: For each person (PID) returns their name, gender, and counts of distinct movies they participated in as cast, director, and producer.
params.when_to_use: Report the number of distinct movies a person has acted in, directed, or produced (per person) | Join person-level movie contribution counts to person demographics or profiles | Filter people by having acted/directed/produced at least N distinct movies | Compose person-level counts into higher-level aggregates (e.g., totals by gender) without double-counting
params.output_schema: PID: unique identifier for a person (from Person.PID) | Name: person's name (from Person.Name) | Gender: person's gender (from Person.Gender) | cast_movie_count: number of distinct movies the person appears in as a cast member (COUNT DISTINCT MID from M_Cast per PID) | director_movie_count: number of distinct movies the person is credited as director (COUNT DISTINCT MID from M_Director per PID) | producer_movie_count: number of distinct movies the person is credited as producer (COUNT DISTINCT MID from M_Producer per PID)
params.grounded_columns: Person.PID | Person.Name | Person.Gender | M_Cast.PID | M_Cast.MID | M_Director.PID | M_Director.MID | M_Producer.PID | M_Producer.MID
params.metric: cast_movie_count = COUNT(DISTINCT M_Cast.MID) GROUPED BY M_Cast.PID (then left-joined to Person.PID; COALESCE to 0 for persons with no cast records) | director_movie_count = COUNT(DISTINCT M_Director.MID) GROUPED BY M_Director.PID (then left-joined to Person.PID; COALESCE to 0) | producer_movie_count = COUNT(DISTINCT M_Producer.MID) GROUPED BY M_Producer.PID (then left-joined to Person.PID; COALESCE to 0)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to Person (this view's base) on PID — safe because this view is one row per Person.PID and represents person-level measures that will not be duplicated when joined to a one-row-per-person table or view (e.g., person profile view). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to other one-row-per-person sibling views such as movie_people_roles (if that view is one row per person) on PID — safe when the sibling is also one row per PID because measures remain one-per-PID. | do NOT naively join this view to any one-to-many movie-level or relationship-level view/table (for example: movie_cast_members, movie_locations, movie_with_genres, movie_with_languages, movie_with_countries, movie_basic) without re-aggregation — joining to a movie-level table on PID (or via movies) will duplicate this view's person-level counts because each person row would be repeated for each matching movie/record. If you need combined data, either: |   - aggregate the movie-level/joined table to one row per PID before joining (e.g., compute movie-level counts or other aggregates grouped by PID), or |   - join this view to movie-level data via a DISTINCT movie key and re-compute counts from the source relationship tables rather than relying on this pre-aggregated measure. | safe composition examples: |   - To get totals by gender: SELECT Gender, SUM(cast_movie_count) FROM people_film_counts GROUP BY Gender — safe because aggregation stays at person grain. |   - To add a person profile: JOIN people_profile pp ON people_film_counts.PID = pp.PID — safe when people_profile is one row per PID. | unsafe composition examples: |   - JOIN people_film_counts pfc ON pfc.PID = movie_cast_members.PID — unsafe if movie_cast_members has one row per (PID,MID) because pfc's counts will be multiplied by each movie row. Re-aggregate movie_cast_members to one-row-per-PID first if combining. |   - JOIN to movie_with_genres or movie_basic without reducing those tables to one row per PID; these are movie-centered and will duplicate person rows.

views.description: Aggregated counts of distinct movies per person for cast, director, and producer roles. One row per PID and role showing counts. Useful to compare activity across roles or to find prolific contributors. | Use for: Who are the most prolific actors/directors/producers; compare counts of movies by person and role; filter persons by minimum movie counts.

views.name: genre_movie_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  g."GID",
  g."Name" AS "Name",
  COUNT(DISTINCT mg."MID") AS "movie_count",
  AVG(m."rating") AS "average_rating",
  SUM(m."num_votes") AS "total_num_votes"
FROM "Genre" g
LEFT JOIN "M_Genre" mg ON g."GID" = mg."GID"
LEFT JOIN "Movie" m ON mg."MID" = m."MID"
GROUP BY g."GID", g."Name"

params.description: Per-genre aggregates: number of distinct movies, average movie rating, and sum of movie vote counts (one row per genre GID).
params.when_to_use: Get counts and summary rating metrics for each genre (e.g., top genres by movie_count or average_rating). | Drive dashboards or reports that compare genres by volume or popularity metrics. | Compose into queries that filter or rank genres, or join genre-level metrics to other one-row-per-genre dimensions.
params.output_schema: GID: genre identifier (derived from Genre."GID"). | Name: genre name (derived from Genre."Name"). | movie_count: number of distinct movies associated with the genre (derived as COUNT(DISTINCT M_Genre."MID")). | average_rating: average of Movie."rating" over movies associated with the genre (derived as AVG(Movie."rating")). | total_num_votes: total votes across movies associated with the genre (derived as SUM(Movie."num_votes")).
params.grounded_columns: Genre."GID" | Genre."Name" | M_Genre."MID" | M_Genre."GID" | Movie."MID" | Movie."rating" | Movie."num_votes"
params.metric: movie_count = COUNT(DISTINCT M_Genre."MID") grouped by Genre."GID" | average_rating = AVG(Movie."rating") grouped by Genre."GID" (NULL when no associated movies with ratings) | total_num_votes = SUM(Movie."num_votes") grouped by Genre."GID" (NULL or 0 depending on DB behavior when no matches)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-genre dimension (e.g., the base Genre table or any normalized genre dimension keyed by Genre."GID") ON Genre."GID" = genre_view.GID — safe because this view is already one-row-per-Genre and such joins are 1:1, so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to other one-row-per-genre views (if present) ON GID — safe for the same reason (1:1 at genre grain). | DO NOT join directly to movie-level tables or any one-to-many detail (for example Movie, M_Genre, movie_with_genres, movie_cast_members, movie_locations, movie_people_roles) without re-aggregation — those joins are 1-to-many from genre to movies or other details and will multiply movie_count, average_rating and total_num_votes. If you need movie-level detail, either (a) join this view to movie-level data only after aggregating the movie-level data back to genre (GROUP BY M_Genre."GID" or Movie."MID" then collapse to genre), or (b) start from the movie-level source and compute new aggregates at the desired grain. | When joining to other aggregate views (e.g., people_film_counts) ensure the other view is at the same grain (one row per GID) or has been aggregated to one row per GID; otherwise re-aggregate post-join to avoid duplicated measures. | If you need to combine these genre metrics with ranking or windowed measures (e.g., movie_rating_rank or movie_running_votes), prefer computing ranks within the same aggregation pipeline or join on GID to rank views that are also one-row-per-GID; do not join to ranking/windowed movie-level views without collapsing them to genre first.

views.description: Aggregate counts and average ratings per genre. One row per GID exposing the genre Name, number of movies in that genre, average rating and total num_votes. Useful for ranking genres by popularity or quality. | Use for: Which genres have the most movies; which genres have highest average rating; genre popularity by votes.

views.name: movie_rating_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "MID",
  "title",
  "year",
  "rating",
  "num_votes",
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "rating" DESC) AS "rating_rank",
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "num_votes" DESC) AS "votes_rank"
FROM "Movie"

params.description: Provides one-row-per-movie ranks and basic movie attributes: rating-based and vote-count-based ranks for each movie.
params.when_to_use: Answering leaderboard questions like 'top N movies by rating' or 'highest-rated movies and their rank'. | Combining movie attributes with other one-row-per-movie facts while preserving the movie-level measures (rating, num_votes) and ranks. | As a base to filter or sort movies by rating_rank or votes_rank before composing additional movie-level joins/aggregations.
params.output_schema: MID: the movie identifier (derived from Movie.MID) | title: the movie title (derived from Movie.title) | year: the movie year (derived from Movie.year) | rating: the movie average rating (derived from Movie.rating) | num_votes: the movie vote count / number of ratings (derived from Movie.num_votes) | rating_rank: RANK() over all movies ordered by rating desc (derived from window expression RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Movie.rating DESC)) | votes_rank: RANK() over all movies ordered by num_votes desc (derived from window expression RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Movie.num_votes DESC))
params.metric: rating_rank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Movie.rating DESC) | votes_rank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Movie.num_votes DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_basic (NORM) on MID — safe because movie_rating_rank is one-row-per-MID and movie_basic is also one-row-per-MID, so measures (rating, num_votes, ranks) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling one-row-per-movie views (e.g., movie_with_languages, movie_with_countries, movie_with_genres) only if those sibling views are implemented as one-row-per-MID (verify their grain). If they are one-row-per-MID, joins on MID are safe and will not duplicate this view's measures. | do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables/views (examples in this DB likely named movie_cast_members, movie_locations, movie_people_roles, movie_with_genres if implemented as many-rows-per-movie) on MID without aggregation first — such joins will duplicate rows and thus multiply movie_rating_rank's measures (rating, num_votes) and invalidate ranks and totals. | If you must combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., movie_cast_members or movie_locations), either: a) aggregate the child to one row per MID before joining (for example, STRING_AGG, COUNT, or other aggregates producing one row per MID), or b) join and then re-aggregate the result, ensuring you apply appropriate aggregations to rating and num_votes (e.g., MAX(rating) or any deterministic rule) and recompute ranks if needed. | Safe composition for analytics pipelines: treat movie_rating_rank as a deterministic, immutable movie-level dimension with measures rating, num_votes, rating_rank, votes_rank. Any join that preserves the 1:1 cardinality on MID is safe; any 1:many join requires an explicit aggregation step to avoid inflating measures.

views.description: Per-movie rank by rating with tie-aware RANK() and also rank by num_votes. One row per MID exposing two rank columns. Useful as a building block for Top-K queries by rating or votes. | Use for: Top-rated movies; most-voted movies; combined filtering by rating_rank or votes_rank.

views.name: movie_running_votes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "MID",
  "title",
  "year",
  "rating",
  "num_votes",
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "year" ASC, "rating" DESC) AS "running_movie_index",
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS "total_movies"
FROM "Movie"

params.description: Provides one row per movie (MID) with static attributes plus a running index ordered by year and rating and the total number of movies.
params.when_to_use: Get movie-level details together with a stable positional index (running order by year ASC, rating DESC) and the total count of movies. | Compose rankings or paginated lists where you need each movie's position in a global ordering and the overall movie count. | Build reports that need movie attributes alongside their rank-like ordinal and a global denominator for percentages.
params.output_schema: MID: unique movie identifier (derived directly from Movie.MID) | title: movie title string (derived directly from Movie.title) | year: movie release year (derived directly from Movie.year) | rating: movie rating (derived directly from Movie.rating) | num_votes: number of votes for the movie (derived directly from Movie.num_votes) | running_movie_index: a 1-based row number computed as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Movie.year ASC, Movie.rating DESC) representing the movie's position in the global ordering by year then rating | total_movies: total count of rows in Movie computed as COUNT(*) OVER () — a global scalar repeated on each row
params.metric: running_movie_index = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Movie.year ASC, Movie.rating DESC) | total_movies = COUNT(*) OVER ()
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional one-row-per-MID views/tables on MID — safe because movie_running_votes is one-row-per-MID so these joins do not duplicate measures. Examples: join to movie_basic on MID, movie_rating_rank on MID (if that view is one-row-per-MID), or any other sibling that is known to be one-row-per-MID. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many views/tables (e.g., movie_with_genres, movie_with_languages, movie_with_countries, movie_cast_members, movie_locations, movie_people_roles) without aggregation, because those contain multiple rows per MID and would duplicate the running_movie_index and total_movies values and multiply measures. If you need attributes from those one-to-many sources, first aggregate them to one row per MID (e.g., array_agg or count/concat) or join to them and then re-aggregate back to MID level to preserve correct cardinality. | When composing metrics that sum or average values from this view, be aware that running_movie_index and total_movies are positional/window expressions repeated per MID; they can be safely used in per-MID calculations. Do not SUM(total_movies) across rows (that would multiply the global count); instead use MAX(total_movies) or take it from any single row as it is constant across all rows. | If joining to aggregate views (e.g., people_film_counts, genre_movie_counts) that are aggregated per a different key (person_id, genre), only join when keys align (e.g., genre to MID only if the aggregate is per MID). Otherwise, re-aggregate or restrict to one-row-per-MID to avoid duplication.

views.description: Running cumulative count of movies ordered by year then rating. One row per movie with a running_movie_index that can be used to select top-N chronologically/quality ordered subsets. Year is kept as provided (text). | Use for: Get first N movies by year then rating; compute percentiles by position; identify position of a movie in chronological/rating order.

views.name: movie_locations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  ml."LID",
  l."Name" AS "Name",
  ml."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Location" ml ON m."MID" = ml."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Location" l ON ml."LID" = l."LID"

params.description: Rows of movie × location mappings: for each movie-location pair it provides the movie id and title, the location id and name, and the mapping row id.
params.when_to_use: List all filming/location entries for movies (movie → location mapping). | Show which movies are associated with a specific location (filter by LID or Name). | Show all locations used by a specific movie (filter by MID or title). | Compose aggregates about movie-location pairs (e.g., count locations per movie) by aggregating this view. | Use as the join input when enriching movie-location pairs with additional movie-level or location-level attributes, provided joins do not duplicate movie-location rows.
params.output_schema: MID: movie identifier, derived from Movie."MID" (base table Movie) | title: movie title, derived from Movie."title" (base table Movie) | LID: location identifier, derived from M_Location."LID" (base table M_Location) | Name: location name, derived from Location."Name" (base table Location); may be NULL if no matching Location row exists (LEFT JOIN) | ID: mapping row identifier from M_Location."ID" (base table M_Location) representing the pk/unique id of the movie-location mapping
params.grounded_columns: Movie."MID" | Movie."title" | M_Location."LID" | M_Location."ID" | Location."Name" | M_Location."MID"
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) over the movie-location grain (not materialized in view) — use COUNT(*) when aggregating this view to count mapping rows | locations_per_movie = COUNT(DISTINCT LID) when aggregated GROUP BY MID (derive from this view by grouping) | movies_per_location = COUNT(DISTINCT MID) when aggregated GROUP BY LID (derive from this view by grouping)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_basic (or any movie-level 1:1 view) on MID — safe because movie_basic is one-row-per-MID and will not duplicate movie-location rows when joined on MID. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_with_genres, movie_with_languages, movie_with_countries, movie_rating_rank, movie_running_votes on MID only if those sibling views are one-row-per-MID; verify their grain (if they are JOINs that produce multiple rows per movie, they are NOT safe). If they are normalized (NORM) or otherwise 1:1, the join is safe. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to Location-level 1:1 views (if present) on LID — safe because location 1:1 enrichment will not duplicate rows. | DO NOT directly join to one-to-many views/tables such as movie_with_genres (if that view is multi-genre-per-movie), movie_cast_members, movie_people_roles, people_film_counts (if representing per-person multiple rows), or any raw tables that are many-per-MID or many-per-LID without aggregation — these joins would multiply movie-location rows and therefore duplicate counts/measures derived from this view. | If you need to combine movie_locations with a one-to-many sibling (e.g., cast members), either: (a) aggregate the one-to-many sibling to the same grain as this view (movie × location) before joining, or (b) aggregate this view to the desired grain (e.g., per-MID) before joining. For example, to get number of cast members per movie-location, first aggregate cast to (MID, LID) or aggregate movie_locations to MID and join to per-movie cast counts. | When composing metrics: re-aggregate after joining to any many-side dataset. For example, to compute locations_per_movie joined with genres, GROUP BY MID and use COUNT(DISTINCT LID) from this view rather than trusting row counts after joining to a multi-genre table. | Key summary: safe to join on MID to any strictly 1:1-per-MID resource and on LID to any strictly 1:1-per-LID resource; do not join without re-aggregation to any resource that is 1:N on MID or LID because that will multiply the movie-location grain and any derived metrics.

views.description: Denormalized movie-to-location relation: one row per movie-location assignment with location Name. Useful for location-based filtering or counts of filming locations. | Use for: List locations for a movie; count movies shot in a location; filter movies by location name.

views.name: movie_people_roles
views.body_sql:
SELECT "MID", "PID", 'cast' AS "role", "ID"
FROM "M_Cast"
UNION ALL
SELECT "MID", "PID", 'director' AS "role", "ID"
FROM "M_Director"
UNION ALL
SELECT "MID", "PID", 'producer' AS "role", "ID"
FROM "M_Producer"

params.description: A flattened union of all person-role assignments on movies (one row per movie-person-role), combining cast, director, and producer relationships.
params.when_to_use: List all people associated with a movie along with their specific role (cast/director/producer). | Compose queries that count or aggregate people-per-movie by role (e.g., number of cast members). | Join movie-level attributes (title, genres, ratings) to people-role assignments to analyze contributors. | Filter movies by a particular person's involvement or by role and then join to other movie-level analytic views.
params.output_schema: MID: movie identifier — derived from base columns M_Cast.MID, M_Director.MID, or M_Producer.MID depending on source union arm | PID: person identifier — derived from base columns M_Cast.PID, M_Director.PID, or M_Producer.PID depending on source union arm | role: role label (literal) — 'cast' | 'director' | 'producer', set by each SELECT in the UNION ALL | ID: relationship id / surrogate id for the assignment — derived from base columns M_Cast.ID, M_Director.ID, or M_Producer.ID depending on source union arm
params.grounded_columns: M_Cast.MID | M_Cast.PID | M_Cast.ID | M_Director.MID | M_Director.PID | M_Director.ID | M_Producer.MID | M_Producer.PID | M_Producer.ID
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) OVER ()  -- not a persisted metric in the view, but any aggregation over rows should be defined by consumers (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY MID, role yields people-per-movie-per-role) | people_per_movie_role = COUNT(PID) GROUP BY MID, role  -- example aggregate consumers will compute from the view rows | distinct_people_per_movie = COUNT(DISTINCT PID) GROUP BY MID  -- example distinct-count aggregate to avoid double-counting when same person appears multiple times in same role (if applicable)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_basic on movie_basic.MID = movie_people_roles.MID — safe because movie_basic is one-row-per-MID (NORM), so it does not duplicate movie_people_roles rows or its counts | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_with_genres / movie_with_languages / movie_with_countries on MID — these sibling views are JOINs that are likely one-to-many (movie_with_genres and movie_with_countries often have multiple rows per movie). Do NOT join them directly if you intend to preserve counts from movie_people_roles (they will multiply rows). Instead, either (a) aggregate movie_with_genres to one row per MID before joining, or (b) join movie_people_roles to movie_basic (one-to-one) and then separately relate genres. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to movie_cast_members on MID or PID only if you understand movie_cast_members' grain — movie_cast_members is a JOIN view and may be one-to-many relative to this view; if movie_cast_members is one-row-per-(MID,PID) it can be safely joined on both keys, but if it contains multiple rows per (MID,PID) (e.g., multiple character records) you must re-aggregate movie_cast_members first to avoid duplicating counts. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to people_film_counts (AGG) on PID — safe because people_film_counts is aggregated by person (one-row-per-PID), so joining preserves movie_people_roles' per-(MID,PID,role) rows without duplication of measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to genre_movie_counts (AGG) or movie_rating_rank (RANK) only after verifying their grain. genre_movie_counts is aggregated by genre or by movie+genre; do not join directly if it is one-to-many to movie — instead pre-aggregate to one row per MID if you need to retain correct counts from this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: do not join movie_people_roles directly to movie_locations or movie_with_genres if those sibling views are many-to-many (movies with multiple locations/genres) without re-aggregation, because such joins will multiply rows and therefore multiply any aggregates computed from movie_people_roles (e.g., counts of people). | general rule: this view's grain is (MID, PID, role) — any dimension or join target that is one-row-per-(MID) or one-row-per-(PID) can be joined safely. Any target that is one-to-many relative to (MID) or (PID) must be reduced to the compatible grain (e.g., aggregated to MID or PID) before joining to avoid duplicating measures.

views.description: Wide relation enumerating people involved in each movie across cast, director, and producer roles. One row per MID/PID/role specifying the role type. Useful for role-based person queries and for unioning different role tables into a single people-in-movie view. | Use for: Find all people associated with a movie across roles; count distinct people per movie; filter people by role type.
